research.process_a: invoices paid by QR Ph or bank transfer that stay open
research.notes: NextPay sells NextInvoice (invoicing) and NextPayout. Own events older than 270 days. CEO Artie Lopez, CTO Don Pansacola — do not name them.

touches.subject: invoices before 31 December
touches.body:
Hi Aldrich,

The BIR e-invoicing deadline on 31 December puts large taxpayers and e-commerce sellers on structured invoices reported within days of a sale. For NextPay's invoicing customers, "paid but the invoice is still open" stops being an annoyance and becomes a compliance gap.

My guess is the hard cases aren't the invoices themselves but the payments around them: a QR Ph or bank transfer that arrives under a different reference, a partial payment, a refund.

We have the base in place: one case per invoice and payment with its full trail, flags when something drifts, and rules tested on past data before they go live. The interesting part is what to build on top, and we want to shape it with a few payments teams on their real data rather than guess.

For NextPay, that could start with replaying last month's invoices against a three-day closing rule. From an export, no integration needed.

Worth trying on invoices, or would returned payouts be the better place to start?

Ilia Frolov
CRO & Product Architect, HAIA
haia.finance
Aldrich, with the BIR e-invoicing deadline on 31 December, I emailed you an idea for NextPay's invoicing side. Would value your view.

Hi Aldrich,

Another angle: returned payouts. The pattern I'd expect is a payout that shows as sent while the supplier says it never arrived, and someone on your team piecing the story together across InstaPay, PESONet and the receiving bank.

The same test works there: replay a month of returned payouts and see which rule would have caught them earlier.

Is that a bigger pain for your customers than invoices?

Ilia

Aldrich, last one from me. If payout operations sit with someone else on the team, who would be best to ask? Happy to reach out directly.

Ilia
